bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Domestic pricing aggression due to post-COVID excess capacity; Delay in ramp-up of new product lines (sampling/validation cycles); Geopolitical uncertainty impacting exports; Government procurement shifts to GeM (e-marketplace) limiting institutional sales growth; Customer stickiness in cell culture requiring long validation periods.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; Acknowledges near-term margin pressure from depreciation and competition; Emphasizes long-term structural growth in biopharma; Transparent about challenges in European organic growth and domestic government tendering.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Reported PAT decline is purely accounting-driven (depreciation) while cash PAT surges ~39%; Domestic government business hampered by GeM mandates forcing L1 (lowest price) buying regardless of quality; Nerbe growth is largely forex-artifact, real organic scale-up paused to prioritize parent capex; Sterilization capability is a strategic moat against single-point failure risks in Eastern India, not just a cost center.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "We remain committed to the long-term growth prospects of the industry and have been investing in the down cycle to strengthen our capacities and capabilities, positioning the company for sustainable growth over the next three to five years."
- Competitive-edge slide claims a "Financial track record with efficient capital allocation & streamlined operations ensuring consistent high profitability"; Key Takeaways cite a "Financial profile with historically healthy EBITDA margin".
- Inorganic capital deployment: "Acquisition of European Entity Nerbe" in 2024, described as "a Hamburg-based distributor specializing in plastic labware products".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Leading market share in India across its addressable labware markets, built over more than four decades of industry presence
- Broad portfolio of over 2,000+ SKUs across 350 product segments spanning consumables, reusables and benchtop instruments
- Vertically integrated manufacturing with in-house product design and development, giving greater control over production processes, quality parameters and operational efficiencies
- Automation-led cleanroom manufacturing - pioneered the first fully robotic cleanroom plant in India for molecular biology consumables; use of medical-grade plastics for critical laboratory applications
- First company in India to commence cell culture manufacturing
- Extensive pan-India distribution network (150+ domestic distributors across 28 states) plus international distribution partnerships reaching 40+ countries through 45+ authorized distributors and partners
- Backward integration into in-house radiation sterilization at Amta, reducing dependence on third-party service providers and improving supply chain control
- Two-pronged international model - branded sales in emerging markets (Asia-Pacific, Middle East, South America) and ODM supply to established players in the US and Europe, leveraging India manufacturing cost competitiveness
- European market access through the acquired German entity Nerbe, an established presence in regulated geographies
- Natural currency hedge - imports raw materials and exports finished goods, partially mitigating forex exposure
- TARSONS brand built on quality, trust and deep sectoral understanding within the life sciences community
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Competition risk — Increased competition from organized and unorganized players may exert pricing pressure and adversely affect profitability. Mitigated through continuous innovation, product differentiation and focused branding and marketing.
- Operational and quality-control risk — Disruptions in manufacturing processes or quality control failures may adversely affect business performance and reputation. Mitigated by automation across production stages, sourcing quality raw materials from established suppliers, and standardized operating and quality control procedures.
- Industry and regulatory risk — Regulatory changes and evolving industry dynamics may create uncertainty and impact operations across markets. Mitigated by ongoing monitoring of regulatory developments and periodic evaluation of compliance frameworks across operating geographies.
- Supplier and raw material price risk — Volatility in raw material prices and supply chain disruptions may affect cost structure and margins. Mitigated by a diversified supplier network, structured sourcing arrangements and annual pricing revisions.
- Liquidity and expansion funding risk — Inability to fund expansion initiatives or meet financial obligations may impact financial standing and market perception - material given the ongoing Panchla and Amta capacity build-out. Mitigated by disciplined liquidity management, strong banking relationships and continuous monitoring of cash flows and financial commitments.
- Foreign exchange risk — Exchange rate fluctuations may impact earnings due to export exposure - exports contributed 31% of total turnover. Partially mitigated by a natural hedge, as the Company imports raw materials and exports finished goods.
- Execution and ramp-up risk on new capacity — The Panchla facility is only in partial commercial production, with remaining commissioning expected by H2 2026-27 and cell culture ramp-up scheduled for the second half of 2026-27; the expected operating leverage depends on utilisation levels improving.
- Concentration - single-state manufacturing and two dominant customer segments — All seven plants and all operations sit in West Bengal, with zero international plants or offices per the BRSR; separately, a significant share of revenue comes from just two customer segments, CROs and the pharmaceutical sector.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Tarsons is in the final stage of a multi-year capacity build-out at two greenfield sites in West Bengal, both on land acquired in 2021 - Panchla (5 acres) and Amta (6 acres). At Panchla, partial commercial production commenced during 2025-26, initially focused on capacity expansion for existing products and the introduction of bioprocess-related products; the facility began contributing to revenues towards the latter part of 2025-26, with a gradual scale-up expected over the coming years. The plant targets liquid handling, bioprocess, cell culture and other new product categories, with the remaining commissioning expected to be completed by H2 2026-27 and cell culture production expected to be ramped up in the second half of 2026-27. Management expects Panchla to broaden the addressable market, strengthen presence in higher-value segments and drive enhanced operating leverage as utilization levels improve. At Amta, the facility - comprising a dedicated fulfilment centre, an in-house radiation sterilization unit and select manufacturing capabilities - was commissioned during 2025-26 and is now fully operational; the radiation sterilization plant was commissioned in August 2025 and the site is currently partially utilized for capacity expansion on selected existing product lines. Bringing sterilization in-house is expected to reduce dependence on external service providers, improve control over critical processes and support operating leverage as volumes scale. Alongside the greenfield sites, the Company increased manufacturing capacity across high-demand categories such as liquid handling, centrifuge ware and cryo ware by investing in additional machines, advanced molds and supporting infrastructure, and continues to deploy advanced automation to reduce manual intervention and raise throughput. Tarsons now operates seven manufacturing facilities, all in West Bengal (Jangalpur, Dhulagarh, Amta, Panchla, Burroshibtolla I, Burroshibtolla II and Kasba), supported by five offices; the BRSR records 7 national plants and 0 international plants. Inorganically, the 2023 acquisition of the Hamburg-based German entity Nerbe added European distribution reach in regulated geographies, and the Company intends to leverage the expanded infrastructure together with Nerbe to deepen its European presence. For 2026-27 the Company aims to leverage its expanded manufacturing capabilities to introduce new products including cell culture and bioprocess products and to strengthen its domestic and international labware presence. The annual report discloses no rupee capex quantum that can be attributed to a period - the capital commitments and segment capital expenditure disclosures supplied were both tagged ambiguous - and it discloses no installed-capacity table in physical units.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Rising healthcare needs, increasing R&D intensity and continued expansion of pharmaceutical, biotechnology and diagnostics ecosystems are creating sustained demand for reliable laboratory solutions
- In India the opportunity is particularly compelling, with the laboratory consumables market expected to expand significantly over the coming years, supported by growing research activity and a progressive healthcare outlook
- Expansion of diagnostics laboratories, contract research organizations and biotechnology research facilities is broadening India's life sciences ecosystem, expected to support demand for laboratory infrastructure, equipment and consumables over the medium term
- Government policy support - the BioPharma SHAKTI programme and higher healthcare budget allocations are expected to create significant opportunities for the healthcare and biopharmaceutical industries
- Global preference is shifting from glassware to laboratory plasticware on superior chemical resistance, durability and cost-efficiency, particularly in high-throughput testing and automated laboratory workflows
- The consumables and disposables segment is growing faster than equipment due to its recurring-use nature and increasing preference for contamination-free single-use workflows
- China+1 supply chain diversification and rebalancing of global production footprints is creating new opportunities for competitive manufacturing destinations such as India
- Panchla progressing towards higher utilization is expected to drive enhanced operating leverage, support portfolio expansion and broaden the addressable market into higher-value segments
- In-house sterilization at Amta is expected to reduce reliance on third-party providers, improve control over critical processes and support operating leverage as volumes scale
- Nerbe deepens access to European markets and enhances distribution capabilities across regulated geographies, complementing the India manufacturing base
- An emerging opportunity in sustainable laboratory consumables - bio-based polymers and recycled plastic labware for environmentally conscious research institutions
- Downside watch-items: escalating geopolitical tensions, trade fragmentation, disruptions to key shipping routes, elevated freight and insurance costs, and commodity/energy price volatility affecting international sourcing networks

currentContext.expansion: Tarsons is in the final stage of a multi-year capacity build-out at two greenfield sites in West Bengal, both on land acquired in 2021 - Panchla (5 acres) and Amta (6 acres). At Panchla, partial commercial production commenced during 2025-26, initially focused on capacity expansion for existing products and the introduction of bioprocess-related products; the facility began contributing to revenues towards the latter part of 2025-26, with a gradual scale-up expected over the coming years. The plant targets liquid handling, bioprocess, cell culture and other new product categories, with the remaining commissioning expected to be completed by H2 2026-27 and cell culture production expected to be ramped up in the second half of 2026-27. Management expects Panchla to broaden the addressable market, strengthen presence in higher-value segments and drive enhanced operating leverage as utilization levels improve. At Amta, the facility - comprising a dedicated fulfilment centre, an in-house radiation sterilization unit and select manufacturing capabilities - was commissioned during 2025-26 and is now fully operational; the radiation sterilization plant was commissioned in August 2025 and the site is currently partially utilized for capacity expansion on selected existing product lines. Bringing sterilization in-house is expected to reduce dependence on external service providers, improve control over critical processes and support operating leverage as volumes scale. Alongside the greenfield sites, the Company increased manufacturing capacity across high-demand categories such as liquid handling, centrifuge ware and cryo ware by investing in additional machines, advanced molds and supporting infrastructure, and continues to deploy advanced automation to reduce manual intervention and raise throughput. Tarsons now operates seven manufacturing facilities, all in West Bengal (Jangalpur, Dhulagarh, Amta, Panchla, Burroshibtolla I, Burroshibtolla II and Kasba), supported by five offices; the BRSR records 7 national plants and 0 international plants. Inorganically, the 2023 acquisition of the Hamburg-based German entity Nerbe added European distribution reach in regulated geographies, and the Company intends to leverage the expanded infrastructure together with Nerbe to deepen its European presence. For 2026-27 the Company aims to leverage its expanded manufacturing capabilities to introduce new products including cell culture and bioprocess products and to strengthen its domestic and international labware presence. The annual report discloses no rupee capex quantum that can be attributed to a period - the capital commitments and segment capital expenditure disclosures supplied were both tagged ambiguous - and it discloses no installed-capacity table in physical units.

- Government policy support - the BioPharma SHAKTI programme and higher healthcare budget allocations are expected to create significant opportunities for the healthcare and biopharmaceutical industries
- Global preference is shifting from glassware to laboratory plasticware on superior chemical resistance, durability and cost-efficiency, particularly in high-throughput testing and automated laboratory workflows
- The consumables and disposables segment is growing faster than equipment due to its recurring-use nature and increasing preference for contamination-free single-use workflows
- China+1 supply chain diversification and rebalancing of global production footprints is creating new opportunities for competitive manufacturing destinations such as India
- Panchla progressing towards higher utilization is expected to drive enhanced operating leverage, support portfolio expansion and broaden the addressable market into higher-value segments
- In-house sterilization at Amta is expected to reduce reliance on third-party providers, improve control over critical processes and support operating leverage as volumes scale
- Nerbe deepens access to European markets and enhances distribution capabilities across regulated geographies, complementing the India manufacturing base
- An emerging opportunity in sustainable laboratory consumables - bio-based polymers and recycled plastic labware for environmentally conscious research institutions
- Downside watch-items: escalating geopolitical tensions, trade fragmentation, disruptions to key shipping routes, elevated freight and insurance costs, and commodity/energy price volatility affecting international sourcing networks

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Tarsons is in the final stage of a multi-year capacity build-out at two greenfield sites in West Bengal, both on land acquired in 2021 - Panchla (5 acres) and Amta (6 acres). At Panchla, partial commercial production commenced during 2025-26, initially focused on capacity expansion for existing products and the introduction of bioprocess-related products; the facility began contributing to revenues towards the latter part of 2025-26, with a gradual scale-up expected over the coming years. The plant targets liquid handling, bioprocess, cell culture and other new product categories, with the remaining commissioning expected to be completed by H2 2026-27 and cell culture production expected to be ramped up in the second half of 2026-27. Management expects Panchla to broaden the addressable market, strengthen presence in higher-value segments and drive enhanced operating leverage as utilization levels improve. At Amta, the facility - comprising a dedicated fulfilment centre, an in-house radiation sterilization unit and select manufacturing capabilities - was commissioned during 2025-26 and is now fully operational; the radiation sterilization plant was commissioned in August 2025 and the site is currently partially utilized for capacity expansion on selected existing product lines. Bringing sterilization in-house is expected to reduce dependence on external service providers, improve control over critical processes and support operating leverage as volumes scale. Alongside the greenfield sites, the Company increased manufacturing capacity across high-demand categories such as liquid handling, centrifuge ware and cryo ware by investing in additional machines, advanced molds and supporting infrastructure, and continues to deploy advanced automation to reduce manual intervention and raise throughput. Tarsons now operates seven manufacturing facilities, all in West Bengal (Jangalpur, Dhulagarh, Amta, Panchla, Burroshibtolla I, Burroshibtolla II and Kasba), supported by five offices; the BRSR records 7 national plants and 0 international plants. Inorganically, the 2023 acquisition of the Hamburg-based German entity Nerbe added European distribution reach in regulated geographies, and the Company intends to leverage the expanded infrastructure together with Nerbe to deepen its European presence. For 2026-27 the Company aims to leverage its expanded manufacturing capabilities to introduce new products including cell culture and bioprocess products and to strengthen its domestic and international labware presence. The annual report discloses no rupee capex quantum that can be attributed to a period - the capital commitments and segment capital expenditure disclosures supplied were both tagged ambiguous - and it discloses no installed-capacity table in physical units.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; Acknowledges near-term margin pressure from depreciation and competition; Emphasizes long-term structural growth in biopharma; Transparent about challenges in European organic growth and domestic government tendering.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Leading market share in India across its addressable labware markets, built over more than four decades of industry presence
- Broad portfolio of over 2,000+ SKUs across 350 product segments spanning consumables, reusables and benchtop instruments
- Vertically integrated manufacturing with in-house product design and development, giving greater control over production processes, quality parameters and operational efficiencies
- Automation-led cleanroom manufacturing - pioneered the first fully robotic cleanroom plant in India for molecular biology consumables; use of medical-grade plastics for critical laboratory applications
- First company in India to commence cell culture manufacturing
- Extensive pan-India distribution network (150+ domestic distributors across 28 states) plus international distribution partnerships reaching 40+ countries through 45+ authorized distributors and partners
- Backward integration into in-house radiation sterilization at Amta, reducing dependence on third-party service providers and improving supply chain control
- Two-pronged international model - branded sales in emerging markets (Asia-Pacific, Middle East, South America) and ODM supply to established players in the US and Europe, leveraging India manufacturing cost competitiveness
- European market access through the acquired German entity Nerbe, an established presence in regulated geographies
- Natural currency hedge - imports raw materials and exports finished goods, partially mitigating forex exposure
- TARSONS brand built on quality, trust and deep sectoral understanding within the life sciences community

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Domestic pricing aggression due to post-COVID excess capacity; Delay in ramp-up of new product lines (sampling/validation cycles); Geopolitical uncertainty impacting exports; Government procurement shifts to GeM (e-marketplace) limiting institutional sales growth; Customer stickiness in cell culture requiring long validation periods.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Reported PAT decline is purely accounting-driven (depreciation) while cash PAT surges ~39%; Domestic government business hampered by GeM mandates forcing L1 (lowest price) buying regardless of quality; Nerbe growth is largely forex-artifact, real organic scale-up paused to prioritize parent capex; Sterilization capability is a strategic moat against single-point failure risks in Eastern India, not just a cost center.
